best_echo_sets.commentary: Offers a 10% unconditional Healing% boost and an most importantly a 15% ATK% boost for the entire team, lasting 30 seconds whenever you heal yourself or any of your allies. This bonus can be triggered by character abilities and weapon effects, is easy to keep active 100% of the time and is a big help for all party members.

main_echo_options.echo_commentary: Simple summon Echo that can be cast any time (ideally right before the wielder's Outro), granting 10% ATK to the team for 20s (sufficient for 2 other teammates' rotation times if cast right before Outro) as well as 10% Energy Regen to the wielder to help with Energy requirements.

best_echo_sets.commentary: Offers a 10% unconditional Energy Regen% boost taking some pressure off your gear when aiming at ER breakpoints. Also upon using Outro, grants the next character switching in a 22.5% ATK boost, amplifying any of your main damage dealers burst windows.

main_echo_options.echo_commentary: Supportive Echo that can be run at the cost of a sizeable chunk of damage for the character who equips, trading personal gain for team benefits. Should always be used and immediately switch cancelled right before performing an Outro, leading to another DPS. When done so will grant the next character switching in 12% increased DMG% which when combined with the 5P Moonlit set which also grants 22.5% ATK% under the same conditions makes for a sizeable boost. While the echo does lower the damage of whoever wears it, it grants a massive chunk of energy on use usually saving 1 or sometimes even 2 Energy Regen sub stats that may otherwise be needed by the wearer allowing for some damage to be recovered.

best_echo_sets.commentary: Offers an unconditional 10% Energy Regen% and 80% Coordinated DMG boost. Also grants a passive supportive effect which triggers when the wearer of this set critically strikes with a Coordinated attack - this effect grants the on field Resonator an ATK% boost regardless if they're the wearer of the set or not.

main_echo_options.echo_commentary: Offers an unconditional 12% Electro DMG and 12% Resonance Skill DMG boost when placed in the Main Echo slot, making it a solid choice for Electro focused resonators who emphasize Resonance Skill damage and are looking to use either the 5P Empyrean Anthem Echo or 5P Void Thunder set bonus.

best_weapons.commentary_details: Xiangli Yao's signature and an ideal weapon for any Resonance Liberation based Gauntlet user. Grants a tremendous 24.3% CRIT RATE boost and 12% generic DMG% boost all permanently and on top of that also grants an incredibly convenient 48% Resonance Liberation DMG% lasting 8 seconds on use of the wearers Liberation. Due to the timing of when this buff activates, it is almost always up when you need it most and the duration can also be extended up to 3 times for 5 seconds each time whenever you use a resonance skill. This extends the total duration of this buff to a whopping 23 seconds.

best_weapons.commentary_details: Free to play accessible alternative for DEF-scaling damage dealers that make use of their Resonance Liberation as a damage dealing tool. A good alternative if you don't have Amity Accord.

best_weapons.commentary_details: An easily accessible supportive option with a reasonable amount of Energy Regen. It also grants the unique ability to gain a sizable chunk of raw Resonance Energy once every 20 seconds. For most character's rotations in teams, this bonus will be ready every time it's their turn to switch-in, making this weapon a great choice for any character who doesn't need damage but needs their Ultimate fast and has trouble accessing it otherwise. The flat energy gain is more powerful the less energy the character and team they are a part of can generate.

cons: Does not provide close to any buffs and is lacking compared to other supports in that department;
Needs to replace his Thunder Wedge often against highly mobile enemies;
Does pretty much literally zero damage unless you're willing to invest hard into him, which has very little return;
Only works in a single team as of patch 1.4 (Jinhsi), where he is not the strongest option, incentivizing investment even less.

Has the shortest rotation time in the game, as he doesn't need to use anything beyond a basic attack, and his skill and echo;
Requires absolutely no investment to perform;
Arguably the easiest character to play, just use basic, skill, echo and swap off;
Provides interruption resistance to the entire team, making all rotations easier to perform;
Makes the stagger bar of enemies easier to shred through;

sections.heading: Summary
paragraphs: Yuanwu is a free 4-star Electro Gauntlet Hybrid character whose main role is to provide buffs to the rest of your team with very low field time. His unique support abilities include a team-wide anti-interruption buff, which makes received enemy attacks not cancel your own, as well as the ability to deal extra Vibration Strength bar damage with his Outro, allowing you to stagger enemies, particularly bosses, and make them vulnerable in short amounts of time.

Yuanwu's skill, replaceable once every 3 seconds, is the core of his gameplay. Summoning a Thunder Wedge that creates a large circular area around itself, it generates Forte gauge for Yuanwu by launching Coordinated Attacks every 1.2 seconds to enemies who take damage within it. Dealing damage based on his DEF, it represents the most important part of his kit and lasts for 12 seconds.

However, once Yuanwu's Forte gauge is filled, which is going to be generated off-field by his Thunder Wedge's coordinated attacks, he can use an enhanced skill that detonates the Thunder Wedge early, dealing a bigger burst of damage based on his DEF. He then enters a state where the rest of his own attacks are empowered. His Ultimate, which deals damage based on his DEF and gives his Forte's enhanced state to the entire team, which in the case of his other teammates grants the Interruption Resistance buff. It also has the Thunder Wedge detonation effect, which greatly helps his generation of Concerto Energy.

All things considered, this makes Yuanwu a character who wants to spend minimal time on the field due to his kit being pretty much exclusively centered around placing his Thunder Wedge down and leaving the field immediately. While he gets enhanced attacks from his Forte's enhanced state, they end up having extremely subpar damage compared to the rest of the cast; all in all, in his single meta use case, you end up pretty much forfeiting this kit entirely.

And now we enter into the main problem with Yuanwu and why he is a low-tier character: presenting subpar damage, and sporting literally no inherent damage buffs in his kit, he does not fill either of the two niches that are required to be a meta character, healing not being necessary due to dodging, healers simply being favoured due to their buffing potential.

As a result, Yuanwu finds himself only one meta niche: being a stack generator for one of the best characters in the game, Jinhsi. Thankfully, he does have Coordinated Attacks that can have 100% uptime, meaning you can infinitely refresh his Thunder Wedge and have it always be ready to hit enemies. As currently the only character in the game that practically does so, he finds value in being the best Forte stack generator for Jinhsi, who capitalizes off of Coordinated Attacks, and finds himself usable sporting the Rejuvenating Glow Echo set and the 3 star weapon Originite: Type IV to allow him to heal himself and trigger the 15% team-wide attack buff the set provides. Only requiring him to add a single Basic Attack to his rotation and simply requiring him to place his Thunder Wedge down and ignore the rest of his kit entirely, he is completely effective to use in Jinhsi teams at level 1 with a 3 star weapon and level 0 echoes, allowing you to invest in your other characters without sacrificing close to any of the team's damage ceiling.

But let's not forget that even in this role, he finds himself doing practically no damage and as a result contributes smaller amounts to the whole team's damage than any option that does. Not to mention that he only has ONE team he properly works in, and requires a very specific build to work (albeit not being an expensive one, it requires you to build your support on a second supportive set, i.e Moonlit Clouds, which is awkward to do in itself).

In summary, this makes Yuanwu usable in a single team, and not useful in many other places. But if you still wish to use him in this role, he is very much recommendable, as his simplistic gameplay makes him very easy to pick up for even the most casual of players.

synergies.commentary: Yuanwu's only meta use case is to work as a good budget option for Jinhsi teams, as he's free to acquire, takes minimal field time, can activate the Rejuvenating Glow set easily with the Originite: Type IV 3 star weapon, and has the highest Coordinated Attack frequency of any character in the game. The pairing isn't meta, but requires minimal investment to perform, and remains a good option.

Make sure to run her with Moonlit Clouds if you're using her along with Yuanwu, as she can trigger her Outro way more consistently & faster than he can every rotation!
